sections.overview: The yellowsnout large-eye bream is a western Pacific lethrinid congener of the Australian Gymnocranius audleyi.
sections.identification: It is silvery with about five to seven narrow, irregular flank bars, a yellow band edged in blue from the eye to the upper lip, and blue cheek stripes. It reaches about 35 cm total length, commonly around 30 cm.
sections.habitat: It lives over sand, mud, or rubble, usually at depths of about 20–80 m, in the Indo-Malaysian Archipelago and South China Sea.
sections.diet: Small bottom-dwelling gastropods form its main reported food.
sections.behavior: The available species accounts describe a reef-associated, non-migratory fish; they provide little detail on social behavior.
sections.reproduction: The consulted catalogue does not give species-specific breeding dates or clutch information.
sections.ecology: It forages on small benthic snails over unconsolidated seabeds, rather than depending on a single coral substrate.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports an IUCN assessment of Least Concern dated 2023.
